headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and associated distribution infrastructure, preventing these costs from being passed on to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Requires Data Centers to Pay for Their Own Power Lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must pay the full cost for the transmission infrastructure they require, preventing these billions of dollars in costs from falling on residential ratepayers. Governor Abigail Spanberger supported this move, which is expected to save Virginia residents hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing state regulators with crucial data for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water resource planners, local communities concerned about water usage, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed SB 553 and HB 496, strengthening water-use reporting requirements for data centers. This legislation aims to provide better data on water consumption by the industry, which can use millions of gallons daily, to aid state and local planners in managing Virginia's water resources.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill mandates site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residences and schools for new high-energy use facilities like data centers, and allows localities to require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forestland.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Delegate Josh Thomas, Senator Danica Roem, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Rules Raise Questions for Construction
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger's executive order and new legislation, including HB 153, are making Virginia more selective about data center development. HB 153 specifically introduces new permitting requirements for high-energy use facilities, mandating sound assessments and allowing localities to require impact analyses on various resources.
